motion.name: progress-slide

motion.name: note-slam

chartPalette.name: The Press Proof Palette
chartPalette.contrastFloor: 3:1 for marks on paper, white, carbon, and carbon-raised. Text never sits in a series hue.
chartPalette.notes: Every filled mark takes its pattern; bars, areas, and radars take a 2px tone stroke, and a pie splits its slices with a 2px ground gap. Every line takes its dash, a square cap, and a 6px point marker (square, hollow square, plus, bar, upright bar). The legend prints the same mark on a paper chip; one press solos a series and a second clears it. Series 04 and 05 are the closest tones and always differ by mark.

focus.name: bracket
focus.value: 3px solid var(--ring) at inset -7px, masked to 10px arms on each side

placements.name: mark
placements.value: 3px solid var(--ring), inset -7px, masked to 10px arms on each side
placements.purpose: A control that stands on the page takes the bracket outside its own edge.

placements.name: row
placements.value: 3px solid var(--ring), inset 0, masked to 10px arms on each side
placements.purpose: A row takes the bracket inside its own border, so it never crosses the rows above and below.

placements.name: clipped card
placements.value: 3px solid var(--ring), inset 0, masked to 10px arms on each side, the card's own rule clearing on focus
placements.purpose: A card at the edge of a clip takes the inside placement, and clears its rule on focus so the bracket reads as a bracket and not as a thick edge.

markStates.disabled: outline 40%, label in muted ink at 5:1 or better in every intent, 3px strike-through

row.rest: paper ground, the words in ink
row.selected: when the row can be selected, the solid ink bar stays and the red foot prints over the row's rule
row.focus: inside bracket on the row's own border
row.disabled: muted words, struck through on the elements that hold the words

markStates.selected: solid fill, paper words, 4px red foot (6px on hover)

knownGaps: The Sonner toast is the one component still on the old structure: it keeps a blur and a soft shadow until its own stage. Do not copy those details from it.

Two glyph languages sit side by side: Note loads its state glyphs from react-icons/hi2, while the Squeeze state marks are drawn as unit SVGs. The plate and the name are shared; the glyph vocabulary is not yet unified.

narrative.overview:
Ritools looks like a note that a person cut from magazines and pinned to a print shop wall. Names are made from cut-out letters on paper chips. All other text is plain print. Hard ink rules divide the page. Three color fields set the structure: a red field for the navbar, an ink field for the side rail, and paper for the content.

The system is flat and loud. It has no soft depth, no rounded corners (the round seal is the one exception), no gradients for depth, and no glass. Contrast, rule weight, and the shape of a mark carry all hierarchy and all state. A control at rest is an outline. When you press it, it fills. When it is disabled, a line strikes through it. When it has keyboard focus, a heavy bracket stands on each side. You can read each state by shape, not only by color.

The density is high but strict. Showcases sit in equal cells on shared 2px rules. Numbers always use one numerals face in fixed columns. Only two diagonal angles occur in drawn shapes: a small tilt and a steeper slash.
keyCharacteristics: Four brand colors: red, ink, paper, and white. The color mode does not change them.
Three grounds: red (navbar), ink (rail), paper (content). A ground redefines the role tokens for what sits on it.
Ransom names from cut-out chips in four display faces. All other text is Archivo.
Martian Mono at 75% width for every number.
Zero radius, except the round seal: opt-in on an icon button, a badge, and an avatar, and always on a radio indicator. No shadows for depth. 2px rules, 3px heavy rules.
Printed-mark states: outline, double outline, solid fill, red foot (selected), strike-through, bracket. An invalid selection prints hollow in a doubled danger rule.
Two angles only in drawn shapes: tilt (4deg) and slash (16deg).
Color mode follows the OS by default. The server render is light.
Overlays print on the page: a flat ink scrim, a 2px rule frame, and a slam from the side they came from. Nothing blurs.

rules.name: The Own-Hue Rule
rules.body: Semantic colors never borrow the brand red. Danger is burnt vermilion, not Poster Red. A red mark means "brand" or "primary action"; it never means "error".

rules.name: The Two-Reds Rule
rules.body: Poster Red fills; Text Red writes. Use `--primary` for fields, fills, and rules. Use `--primary-ink` for red words on paper or carbon.

rules.name: The Hollow Invalid Rule
rules.body: A selected control that is invalid never fills with danger: a danger fill next to a red mark changes only the hue. It prints hollow: no fill, no foot, the edge doubled in danger (an inset 2px second rule), and its numeral or glyph in the danger wash ink. This holds for dates, range ends, checkboxes, radios, and choice box options.

rules.name: The Wash Ink Rule
rules.body: A status tone is carried by its wash foreground, never by its fill hue. The fill hues are for fields: Caution Yellow never reaches 3:1 on paper. A note takes the wash ink for its frame, a meter takes it for its fill, a tracker block takes it for its plate.

rules.name: The Ground Rule
rules.body: A color field redefines the role tokens for its children (`.ground-red`, `.ground-ink`). On red, the primary becomes white, rules become white, and the red chip becomes ink. On ink, rules become paper and the ink chip lifts to Carbon Chip. Put a stock control on a ground; do not add new props for it.

rules.name: The Proof Mark Rule
rules.body: A chart series is named by a tone and a proof mark. Five series never depend on color: every fill carries a pattern, every line a dash, and the legend prints the same mark. The two closest tones (04 and 05) always differ by mark. A chart is a proof sheet, not a color wheel.

rules.name: The Ransom Rule
rules.body: Ransom is only for names: Component Entry titles, Category headings, the Ritools wordmark, Tool names, the title of a pinned note (a dialog, a sheet, a drawer), and Squeeze outcome words at poster scale (for example the all-miss "Miss"). Never use it for labels, inputs, numbers, or body text. Assistive technology reads the plain name, never the chips. In the Squeeze ledger, where an outcome must read at a glance across a hundred rows, the five outcomes (Done, Already fits, Miss, Bigger, Rejected) take the Poster Title voice at 0.875rem instead; the word and its state mark carry the row.

rules.name: The One Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every number uses the `num` utility: Martian Mono, 75% width, tabular figures, slashed zero. Numbers sit in fixed columns (for example a `3ch` width for catalog counts) so they do not shift when they change.

rules.name: The Same Cut Rule
rules.body: One text always cuts the same way. A stable hash of the text seeds the face, chip, tilt, lift, and scissor cut of each letter, so the server and the client render the same note.

rules.name: The Strict Grid Rule
rules.body: Showcases sit in equal cells on shared 2px rules. Do not float cards, add gaps between cells, or let a cell grow its own height style.

rules.name: The Print Has No Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If two surfaces must separate, use a rule or a field change, never a shadow or blur.

rules.name: The Two Angles Rule
rules.body: A drawn diagonal is 4deg or 16deg. Icon glyphs keep their own drawing.

rules.name: The Inside Bracket Rule
rules.body: A row takes the bracket inside its own edge, not 7px outside it: a 3px bracket with 10px arms at each side, drawn on the row's own border. An outside bracket would cross the rows above and below. A card that sits at the edge of a clip takes the same inside placement, and it clears its own rule on focus, so the bracket stands clear instead of thickening the edge.

rules.name: The Reach Rule
rules.body: A bar that ranks values takes the slider's reach: a 2px Control Edge rule with a 4px ink stroke over it, so the value reads by weight and not by hue. A bar-list row and a leaderboard row use it, and the figure stays in a fixed column beside it.

rules.name: The Ink Measure Rule
rules.body: A measure fills with ink. A status hue arrives only when the caller asks for one, and then the caller owns the word that names it. The progress bar is the one brand measure and fills with Poster Red. The figure beside a measure is in the one numerals face, in a fixed 6-character column.

rules.name: The Strike on the Words Rule
rules.body: A disabled row is muted and struck through, and the strike is drawn on the elements that hold the words. A text decoration does not cross a block box, so a strike on the row alone would print on the row's own line and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Paper Side Rule
rules.body: A badge on a solid ink bar turns to the paper side: the border and the words take the bar's foreground, and the badge's own wash clears.

rules.name: The Local Poster Rule
rules.body: An empty result reuses the poster page at a local scale: the numeral `0` in the numeral-display voice, a 16deg red slash bar, and one line of words.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: A table draws its rules per cell, with separated borders, so a row rule and a column rule never collapse into one another. The red foot of a selected row prints on the cell, over its own rule.

dos: Do put names in Ransom and everything else in Archivo. Give every Ransom its plain name for assistive technology.
Do use `--primary` (Poster Red) for fills and rules, and `--primary-ink` (Text Red) for red words.
Do put white text on the red field. Small text on red is never ink.
Do set every number with the `num` utility, in a fixed-width column.
Do show every control state by shape: outline, double outline, solid fill, red foot, strike-through, bracket.
Do use a ground class (`ground-red`, `ground-ink`) to place stock controls on a color field.
Do separate surfaces with 2px rules (3px for the heaviest divisions) or with a field change.
Do use 4deg for tilts and 16deg for slashes and cuts.
Do draw the focus bracket inside a row, on the row's own border, so it never crosses the rows above and below.
Do separate an overlay from the page with the ink scrim, and separate a surface inside it with a 2px rule.
Do carry a status tone in its wash foreground, never in its fill hue.
Do keep reduced motion in the composed end state: chips assembled, popovers in place, loaders still.
Do follow the OS color mode by default, and render light on the server.
donts: Don't use Poster Red or Text Red for errors or other semantic states. Danger is burnt vermilion.
Don't let red be the only signal for a state.
Don't fill a selected control with danger when it is invalid. Print it hollow in a doubled danger rule.
Don't fade a disabled label's hue. Use muted ink, and let the strike carry the state.
Don't round a corner, except the round seal: an icon button with `isCircle`, a radio indicator, a badge with `isCircle`, and an avatar with `isSquare={false}`.
Don't add shadows, blur, glass, or gradients for depth.
Don't draw a diagonal at any angle other than 4deg or 16deg.
Don't use Ransom for labels, inputs, numbers, buttons, or body text.
Don't use a second numerals face, or proportional figures for numbers.
Don't load fonts from a CDN. Fonts are self-hosted and open-licensed.
Don't bring back the IntentUI look: Inter, blue primary, zinc grays, rounded cards, soft focus glows.
Don't give a popover or a tooltip a triangle arrow. It takes the square tab.
Don't treat the Sonner toast as part of this system. It is the one component still on the old structure, with a blur and a soft shadow, and it waits for its own stage.
